title: Einstein's cosmological constant and cosmic antigravity
summary: Avi Loeb tells of Einstein's cosmological constant and cosmic antigravity, about 1917-present at universe, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: Einstein liked the idea that the universe never expanded because then you don't have to imagine what was there before the beginning.

plain: Avi Loeb, a Harvard astrophysicist, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about the cosmological constant, a term Albert Einstein added to his gravity equations in 1917 that works like a kind of cosmic antigravity. Loeb says Einstein liked the idea of a universe that never expanded, because then nobody has to imagine what came before the beginning.
